panic.format: pthread kernel extension not loaded (function table is NULL). @%s:%d
panic.reading: bsd_init calls pthread_init(); it panics unless the pthread kext has called pthread_kext_register() to fill _pthread_functions
panic.format_captured_automatically: The fixture now reads the panic format string from x0 itself and records it as panic_format, so a run explains its own panic without a separate --read-at.

finding: A multiprocessor emulated machine gets past the GIC target probe: gicv2::Controller::prepareLocal is reached (it was not with --smp 1), the kernel enters bsd_init -- a milestone this port had never reached -- and then panics with 'pthread kernel extension not loaded (function table is NULL)'. The linked image does contain _pthread_functions, _pthread_kext_register and the pthread kext symbols, so the gap is that the kext never starts and registers, not that it is missing from the link.
corrected_earlier_reading: QEMU's hw/intc/arm_gic.c returns 0 for the whole target register range only when num_cpu == 1 ('For uniprocessor GICs these RAZ/WI'); with two or more CPUs it reports cm for the banked SGI/PPI range. The handset GIC is multiprocessor, so the ArmCpu probe is probably correct on hardware: the earlier note that it 'may be wrong on the handset too' was wrong.
not_proven: XNU entry or iOS userland on a handset
that the pthread kext can be started on this port (its dependencies are unexamined)
anything about the eMMC, display or GPU on real hardware

prelink_closure._note: from out/lumia950/kernel/kernel.json in the kernel artifact of run 44003233713
prelink_closure.reading: board.toml [kernel.prelink] roots names four kernelcache components; the prelink adds what those declare as libraries. The pthread kext is not a library of any of them, so it is not in the closure, its start routine never runs, pthread_kext_register() is never called, and _pthread_functions stays NULL.

next_action: configs/lumia950_defconfig now sets CONFIG_XNU_SOURCE_PTHREAD=y, guarded by scripts/test-native-bringup.py::test_the_pthread_provider_must_stay_in_the_configuration. The fix is not yet verified in an image: linking the source component needs the macOS kernel job, which currently does not start. When it does, the run should show bsd_init returning and the panic string changing.

root_cause.framework_effect: builds build/libpthread-kernel/libpthread_kernel.a and registers it: patches/xnu/source-pthread-bootstrap.patch adds STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_SECOND, source_pthread_bootstrap), which calls pthread_start() so _pthread_functions is filled before bsd_init
root_cause.image_evidence: the linked image contains _pthread_functions and _pthread_kext_register (the xnu shims) but neither pthread_start nor source_pthread_bootstrap, so the source component was never built or linked
root_cause.why_not_the_kext: the prelink closure is roots plus their declared libraries; the pthread kext is nobody's library dependency, so it can never arrive that way

past_bsd_mode._note: measured locally with --past-bsd against the same kernel artifact, the mode the CI observation step now uses
past_bsd_mode.reading: The mode keeps observing after bsd_init instead of stopping at its entry, so a run reports whether bsd_init returns, whether vfs_mountroot is reached, and the panic text when it is not. With the current kernel the answer is: it enters bsd_init, never returns, never reaches mountroot, and panics on the pthread table.

findings: All FIPSPOST_KEXT tests report PASSED and 'corecrypto_kext_start completed successfully' before the panic: the source crypto POST is not only returning 0 to the fixture, it is in the kernel's own record.
initialize_screen reports the DarwinBoot framebuffer (0x6C7A0000, 800x600, row 3200) as the kernel's screen, so a framebuffer console has a place to write after ExitBootServices.
ml_processor_register registers exactly one processor, cpu_number 0, which matches the single-CPU ADT profile.
pe_arm_init_debug: failed to initialize gSocPhys == 0 is logged during interrupt controller bring-up. It is a warning, not the stop.
the log ends at 'mbinit: done', i.e. inside the BSD start, which is where the pthread panic happens.
kernel_log.why_it_matters: This is the content the log transport (P1.1) exists to carry. On the emulator it can be read straight out of kernel memory; on a handset it still needs a way out, which is what the GOP-first decision record is about.
